sarah: Quick perf note — ran a 1h soak on the new batcher variant. Profiler shows a p99 decode spike right after large prefill bursts (prefill sizes > 1k tokens). Flame (top lines):
```
gpu_kernel__matmul_fused_fp16  42%
gpu_kernel__attention_kv         18%
gpu_kernel__softmax              9%
kv_cache_lookup_miss_rate        7%
other (memcpy, scheduling)      24%
```
Also saw queue wait times jump on the decode queue while prefill queue was draining. Opening thread to discuss ideas for phase separation + token allocator.

ahmed: Can you paste the raw numbers for queue wait times + token budgets? curious about burst pattern.

sarah: Sure — simplified:
```
prefill: avg wait 6ms, 99th 120ms, tokens per req avg 900
decode: avg wait 3ms, 99th 340ms, tokens per req avg 40
KV cache miss rate spikes to 11% for requests that hit decode after a heavy prefill burst
```
We were using a single global token_budget=150 and a unified FIFO sequencer. When prefill burst hits, it grabs most of the budget and decode tasks pile up.

linh: This matches what I saw in the microbenchmarks — prefill tends to be long-tail token consumers and should not starve decode. Proposal: separate queues + a phase-aware sequencer that maintains two token_budgets: budget_prefill and budget_decode. Sequencer logic: prefer decode if decode_wait > X ms or decode_queue_length > Y, otherwise round-robin. Also add a warmup window where newly started prefill requests are rate-limited for first N tokens to avoid sudden KV pressure.

derek: Sketch of sequencer pseudocode (very rough):
```
while true:
  if decode_queue.len > decode_high or decode_wait > decode_wait_high:
    allocate tokens = min(budget_decode, next_decode_req.remaining)
  else if prefill_queue.len > 0:
    allocate tokens = min(budget_prefill, next_prefill_req.remaining)
  else:
    allocate tokens = min(global_min_budget, next_any.remaining)
```
Add backpressure: if kv_miss_rate > threshold -> reduce budget_prefill by 30% until stable.

ahmed: Love the warmup idea. Two quick caveats: 1) kernel selection needs to be phase-aware — decode should pick low-latency fused kernels even if they use slightly more GPU memory, 2) make sure autoscale doesn't treat split queues as independent capacity units (we still want overall GPU utilization).

sarah: Experimented with a prototype yesterday — changed sequencer to give decode a floor of 40 tokens per round and limited prefill max-chunk to 256 during warmup. Results from the canary run: p95 decode latency -12%, p99 decode latency -28%, overall GPU utilization -3% (acceptable). KV miss spikes reduced from 11% -> 4%.

linh: Do you have the exact config you tested? can we reproduce?

sarah: config snippet:
```
sequencer:
  decode_floor_tokens: 40
  prefill_max_chunk_warmup: 256
  warmup_duration_sec: 8
  kv_miss_backoff_threshold: 0.08
  kv_backoff_fraction: 0.3
kernel_selector:
  prefer_low_latency_for_phase: [decode]
```
Deployed via: `./deploy/batcher_canary.sh --variant phase_split --pct 5`

deploy-bot: deploy started for batcher_canary phase_split at 2026-03-10T14:22:11Z — target 5% traffic. CI green.

derek: Nice numbers. Two questions: 1) did you observe any workload classes where decode still starved? 2) any perf regression for short-prefill workloads?

sarah: 1) Some tiny residual starvation on pathological mixes (lots of interleaved short prefill + decode within same session) — I think per-session affinity to avoid interleaving might help. 2) short-prefill (<=64 tokens) actually improved slightly because prefill max-chunk prevented big prefill monopolies. No regressions in p95 overall.

linh: For kernel selector, I'll land a small change to bias the kernel table when request.phase == decode. It will add a tiny rule: if seq_len < 128 prefer fused matmul kernel version v2_fp16_lowlat. I'll open a PR with benchmark numbers.

ahmed: Also add a KV-aware drain: before switching a GPU lane from prefill to decode, check per-shard kv_warmth score and prefer lanes with higher warmth for rapid decode hits. That will reduce cold-miss penalty.

sarah: Agreed. Next steps I propose:
- Linh: kernel selector patch + bench (owner: linh)
- Derek: implement sequencer pseudocode + unit tests (owner: derek)
- Ahmed: KV-warmth metric + backpressure hook (owner: ahmed)
- Sarah: roll canary to 20% after PRs merge, collect 24h metrics, focus on p99 decode and kv_miss_rate
Anyone object? :thumbsup:

derek: +1
linh: +1
ahmed: +1

sarah: Thanks everyone — I'll post a short follow-up with exact alerts to watch (p99 decode > 200ms, kv_miss_rate > 8%, gpu_util < 60% for 10m).
